harvestMethod: Cut stems above a leaf node once plants reach 15cm. Regular harvesting encourages bushy growth.
growingNotes: Full sun. Drought-tolerant once established. Pinch flowers to keep producing leaves.

harvestMethod: Snip sprigs as needed. Best harvested just before flowering for strongest flavour.
growingNotes: Full sun. Excellent drainage essential. Let soil dry between waterings.

harvestMethod: Cut leaves at base, leaving 5cm. The purple flowers are edible too.
growingNotes: Sun to part shade. Consistent moisture. Divide clumps if they get crowded.

harvestMethod: Pinch above a leaf pair. Never let it flower — pinch buds immediately.
growingNotes: Full sun, warm soil. Very frost-sensitive. Water consistently but don't soak.

harvestMethod: Cut outer stems at the base. The plant will keep producing from the centre.
growingNotes: Sun to part shade. Keep moist. Slow to germinate — be patient.

harvestMethod: Cut outer leaves when 15cm tall. Let some bolt for coriander seeds.
growingNotes: Part shade in summer. Bolts quickly in heat — succession sow every 3 weeks.

harvestMethod: Snip fronds as needed. Harvest seeds when heads turn brown.
growingNotes: Full sun. Doesn't transplant well — direct sow only. Attracts beneficial insects.

harvestMethod: Pick outer leaves when 7–10cm. Baby leaves are milder.
growingNotes: Part shade in summer. Fast growing — harvest within 30–40 days. Succession sow.

harvestMethod: Pick when fully coloured and slightly soft. Cherry tomatoes ripen fast in clusters.
growingNotes: Full sun, 8+ hours. Stake or cage. Prune suckers for larger fruit. Heavy feeder.

harvestMethod: Cut for bouquets when petals are just opening. Vase life 7–10 days.
growingNotes: Full sun. Good drainage. Rotate — don't plant in same soil two years running.

pretreatment: Refrigerate seeds 7 days before sowing. Needs darkness to germinate — cover completely.
harvestMethod: Pick flowers for salads. Deadhead for continuous blooming through cool weather.
growingNotes: Part shade to full sun. Cool-weather flower — may fade in July heat, revives in autumn.

pretreatment: Cold stratify 7–14 days in fridge before sowing.
harvestMethod: Cut spent flower spikes to encourage a second bloom. Excellent cut flower.
growingNotes: Full sun. Stake tall varieties. Protect from strong winds. Rich, moist soil.

pretreatment: Soak seeds 24h + lightly scarify with sandpaper. Caution: seeds are toxic.
harvestMethod: Deadhead spent spikes for possible rebloom. Let some go to seed if you want volunteers.
growingNotes: Full sun. Doesn't need rich soil — fixes its own nitrogen. Deep taproot — deep pot essential.

harvestMethod: Harvest leaves and flowers. Unlike sweet basil, tulsi flowers are desirable — harvest them for tea.
medicinalProperties: Adaptogenic herb. Used in Ayurveda for stress relief, immune support, and respiratory health. Make fresh tea from leaves and flowers.
growingNotes: Full sun. Warmth-loving. Slightly more tolerant of cool nights than sweet basil.

pretreatment: Surface sow — needs light to germinate. Press gently, don't cover.
harvestMethod: Harvest roots in autumn of second year. Flowers and leaves are fine; the root is the medicinal part.
medicinalProperties: Root used as sleep aid and anxiety reducer. Dried root can be made into tea or tincture. Very potent — use with care.
growingNotes: Sun to part shade. Moist soil. Can grow tall (1m+) — may need staking. Attracts cats.
safetyNote: Valerian root — keep out of reach. The flowers and leaves are fine; it's the root that's potent.

pretreatment: Surface sow — needs light. Very fine seeds — barely press in.
harvestMethod: Cut flower heads when fully open for drying. Leaves can be harvested anytime.
medicinalProperties: Traditional wound herb. Anti-inflammatory. Tea from flowers and leaves for fever and cold symptoms.
growingNotes: Full sun. Very drought-tolerant. Lean soil is fine — too rich makes it floppy.

pretreatment: Cold stratify 7–14 days OR surface sow. Needs light. Slow and erratic germination.
harvestMethod: Cut stems when flowers just begin to open. Bundle and hang to dry.
medicinalProperties: Calming, anti-anxiety. Essential oil for sleep. Tea from flowers. Sachets for linens.
growingNotes: Full sun. Excellent drainage critical. Don't overwater. Sandy/gritty soil preferred.

pretreatment: Cold stratify 7 days in fridge. Keep dark during germination — use 16-tray.
harvestMethod: Harvest flowers and upper leaves at peak bloom. Roots after 3+ years.
medicinalProperties: Immune-boosting. Tea from fresh or dried flowers and leaves. Traditional cold and flu remedy.
growingNotes: Full sun. Drought-tolerant once established. Don't over-fertilize.

pretreatment: Surface sow — needs light. Mist only, don't water heavily.
harvestMethod: Pick flower heads when petals reflex downward. Dry for tea.
medicinalProperties: Classic calming tea. Anti-inflammatory. Good for digestive upset and sleep. Safe for children in mild doses.
growingNotes: Full sun to part shade. Doesn't need rich soil. Self-seeds readily.

harvestMethod: Cut outer leaves at base, leaving inner leaves to grow. Baby leaves in 30 days, full size in 55–60.
growingNotes: Sun to part shade. Consistent moisture. Beautiful coloured stems — ornamental and edible.

harvestMethod: Pinch stems above a leaf node. Purple flowers are attractive and edible.
growingNotes: Full sun. Heat-loving. Anise/licorice flavour. Excellent in stir-fries and curries.

pretreatment: Surface sow. Low germination rate (30–50%) — sow all 30 seeds. Be very patient.
harvestMethod: Snip woody stems. Harvest regularly to shape. Flavour intensifies as it matures.
growingNotes: Full sun. Sandy, well-draining soil. Very drought-tolerant. Slow grower from seed.

pretreatment: Cold stratify 7–10 days in fridge before sowing.
harvestMethod: Pick leaves as needed. Flower buds are edible. Large leaves great for wrapping.
growingNotes: Full sun to part shade. Japanese herb — perilla family. Fresh, minty-basil flavour.

pretreatment: Surface sow — needs light. Tiny seeds.
harvestMethod: Cut stems freely — it's unstoppable. Best flavour just before flowering.
medicinalProperties: Digestive aid. Tea from fresh leaves for nausea, headaches, and congestion. Very safe.
growingNotes: Sun to shade. MUST be isolated — spreads aggressively. Never plant with other herbs.

harvestMethod: Pick outer leaves for baby spinach in 25–30 days. Full rosettes in 45–50 days.
growingNotes: Part shade in summer. Cool-weather crop — bolts in heat. Start early, succession sow.

harvestMethod: Pick flowers regularly to encourage more blooms. Dry petals for tea and salves.
medicinalProperties: Skin-healing. Infused oil for salves and creams. Anti-inflammatory. Edible petals add colour to salads.
growingNotes: Full sun. Easy grower. Self-seeds. Deadhead for continuous blooms.

harvestMethod: Cut-and-come-again: harvest outer leaves. Or cut whole head at base.
growingNotes: Part shade in summer. Keep consistently moist. Bolts in heat — shade cloth helps.

harvestMethod: No harvest needed — ground cover and pollinator plant. Trim if leggy to encourage reblooming.
growingNotes: Full sun to part shade. Spills beautifully over edges. Attracts beneficial insects.

pretreatment: Soak seeds 12–24 hours before sowing. Direct sow after last frost.
harvestMethod: Pick flowers, leaves, and seed pods — all edible. Peppery flavour.
growingNotes: Full sun. Poor/lean soil preferred — too rich = all leaves, few flowers. Trails beautifully.

harvestMethod: Deadhead spent blooms for continuous flowering. Natural pest deterrent.
growingNotes: Full sun. Easy and reliable. Repels aphids and whiteflies near tomatoes.

harvestMethod: Pick lower leaves first, leaving the growing tip. Flavour improves after light frost.
growingNotes: Sun to part shade. Cool-weather crop. Very hardy — survives light frost. Good fall crop.

pretreatment: Surface sow — needs light. NO heat pad. Use 16-tray.
harvestMethod: Cut stems for bouquets. Deadhead for continuous blooming. Excellent cut flower.
growingNotes: Full sun. Cool-weather flower — peak in spring and fall. May pause in summer heat.
